purpose: The ONE definition of 'a TypeScript-shaped token that massu must not ship to every stack'. Read by scripts/measure-asset-conformance.sh (P1, the measurement) and by packages/core/src/__tests__/stack-asset-conformance.test.ts (P4, the gate). Two instruments that judge the same property must not carry two definitions of it — that is the drift this plan exists to end (G32/CR-74).
oracle: THIS IS AN ORACLE AND MAY NEVER BE DERIVED (G32 option 0). It is a guard's EXPECTATION of the answer, not data the system uses. Derived from the assets it judges, both sides would agree by construction and the gate would pass forever (THE BLIND-GATE LAW). Every entry is a judgement someone made, and carries its reason.
halves: The partition is load-bearing: P4.1's TOOLCHAIN/PROSE split is DERIVED from which half matched, never from a second hand-written list. An asset matching only `vocabulary` is TOOLCHAIN — the stack contract can express it, so it gets migrated. An asset matching `prose` is PROSE — it is massu's OWN repo layout leaked into the product, no vocabulary can fix it, and it needs a rewrite, a variant file, or an explicit per-site exemption.

vocabulary.reason: TypeScript's type checker invoked directly. Expressible as {{verify.type}}, which resolves to `mypy .` on python-fastapi and `go vet ./...` on go-chi.
The npm test runner. Expressible as {{verify.test}}. On a Python stack npm does not exist, so this check cannot run and reports nothing — the blind gate this plan exists to close.
Expressible as {{verify.build}}, which is OPTIONAL: only 4 of 13 stacks resolve a primary-language `build`, so a naive substitution throws on 9.
massu's own test framework name. Expressible as {{verify.test}}; naming the framework rather than the command hardcodes the JS ecosystem.
The Turborepo task runner. Expressible as {{verify.test}} / {{verify.type}}; assumes a JS monorepo that 12 of 13 stacks are not.

prose.reason: massu's OWN monorepo layout. A customer's source lives at {{paths.source}} — `app` on python-fastapi, `internal` on go-chi, `Sources` on swift-ios. No vocabulary substitution makes this sentence true for them.
massu's MCP tool-registration file. Instructions about wiring a tool into tools.ts are about developing massu, not about the customer's repo.
A TypeScript project file. Present in 2 of 13 stacks; naming it presumes a toolchain most customers do not have.
massu's hook bundler. A customer never invokes it; referencing it describes massu's build, not theirs.
A Node native dependency of massu's own storage layer. Naming it in a shipped asset leaks an implementation detail of the product into the customer's instructions.
